evidence: Sall. J. 2.2: ingeniī facinora, sīcut anima, immortālia sunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The breath of life, and the soul that outlives the body (Sall.); the Church’s word for the soul (Magnificat anima mea Dominum). The plural’s dative and ablative are animīs, in the Church also animābus (Lewis & Short).
The thinking and feeling soul, the mind; anima is the soul as life itself (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: angusta est domus animae meae quō veniās ad eam: dīlātētur abs tē. ruīnōsa est: refice eam
phrases.english: the house of my soul is too small for you to come into: let it be enlarged by you. It is falling down: rebuild it

sources: Lewis & Short: anima · Lewis & Short: animus
